evidence: Quint. 1.7.3: eadem littera nōminātīvō cāsū brevis, ablātīvō longa est
terms.comment: Short for cāsus nōminātīvus, the naming case; the adjective may stand alone. Quintilian also calls it the upright case, rēctus cāsus (1.5.61).

evidence: Quint. 1.5.61: masculīna Graeca nōmina rēctō cāsū

phrases.latin: cum eadem littera nōminātīvō cāsū brevis, ablātīvō longa est
phrases.english: when the same letter is short in the nominative and long in the ablative

sources: Lewis & Short: nominativus · Lewis & Short: rectus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 221, 240, 247.
